notes.title: Quartet arrives to Kickstarter!
notes.notes:
[h1]QUARTET ARRIVES TO KICKSTARTER[/h1]
[h2]Classic turn-based indie RPG with tag-team mechanics [/h2]

[b]September 1st, 2021[/b]: Quartet, the second retro-inspired JRPG from games studio Something Classic, is live on Kickstarter now until September 30th, 2021.  A spiritual successor to Something Classic’s 2017 release, Shadows of Adam, Quartet lets players control eight characters across four stories that gradually merge into one epic quest.  Backers on Kickstarter can opt into a variety of rewards, from copies of the game to higher-level rewards like the chance to design epic gear, craft an NPC, or even write a whole quest!  Join the campaign: [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/somethingclassic/quartet-0]https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/somethingclassic/quartet-0[/url]

[i]“Shadows of Adam was a success for us,” [/i]says producer Tyler Mire.  [i]“But we learned so much from the experience and the user feedback. We’ve put everything we’ve learned into Quartet to make it so much bigger and better than our last game.”[/i]

From the steampunk-inspired streets of Leornia, to the airship battles that rage on the battlefront of the Auslen Empire, Quartet takes players on an adventure they will never forget!  Meet a remarkable cast of characters including a snooty mage, a disillusioned soldier, an irreverent cook, a troubled shop girl, a sentient water mammal, a dashing doctor, a magical cop, and an ancient golem.  Collect oodles of powerful gear for your small army of protagonists, while unraveling an ancient conspiracy that literally reshaped the world centuries ago.

[b]Features include:[/b]
[list]
[*] Eight heroes with a unique roster of spells and abilities
[*] Tactically deep tag-team combat
[*] A sprawling, character-driven story
[*] Tons of epic and imaginative loot
[/list]

[b]ABOUT QUARTET[/b]
Quartet begins with four separate chapters, playable in any order.  In those four chapters, players meet eight unlikely heroes, and get to see how the stories intertwine into an epic narrative surrounding the war over the control of magic.  In battle, players deploy four characters at any time, with the ability to instantly swap the other four characters in, tag-team style.

[b]ABOUT SOMETHING CLASSIC[/b]
Something Classic is an indie studio with a passion for modern takes on the classic JRPG genre.  Their previous game, Shadows of Adam, was a cult hit among retro JRPG enthusiasts and is available on Steam, Nintendo Switch and Sony Playstation 4.

Quartet is on Kickstarter from September 1st 2021 through September 30th 2021 at [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/somethingclassic/quartet-0]https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/somethingclassic/quartet-0[/url]

Shadows of Adam Coming to PlayStation with a Limited Collector’s Edition
Long-awaited physical edition pre-orders now open for Switch and PlayStation

Los Angeles -  June 14th, 2021 | PM Studios and Something Classic Games are pleased to announce that the indie classic Shadows of Adam is coming to PlayStation 4 digitally and on Nintendo Switch in physical form. The digital PlayStation 4 version will be launching tomorrow, June 15th and in addition, pre-orders begin tomorrow for the physical versions via Limited Run Games for both PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch.

https://youtu.be/yialDpOnj90

Digital pre-orders can be placed via the PlayStation Store for $14.99. Limited physical editions will be available at Limited Run Games for $34.99 and $64.99.

Pre-orders go live Tuesday, June 15th at 12 Noon EST via Limited Run Games and can be ordered via the following links..
Shadows of Adam [PlayStation 4] - 1,500 units: https://limitedrungames.com/products/shadows-of-adam-ps4
Shadows of Adam [PlayStation 4 Limited Edition] - 500 units https://limitedrungames.com/products/shadows-of-adam-collectors-edition-ps4
Shadows of Adam [Nintendo Switch] - 4,000 units https://limitedrungames.com/products/shadows-of-adam-switch
Shadows of Adam [Nintendo Switch Limited Edition] - 1,000 units https://limitedrungames.com/products/shadows-of-adam-collectors-edition-switch

Shadows of Adam is a creative, humorous and exciting take on the 16-bit JRPG era, but with its own twists and style for the modern day gamer. Fast-paced battles, gorgeous graphics, an awesome soundtrack and the convenience to save anywhere you like make it tough to resist! Whether playing on the TV or in handheld mode, the game’s glorious pixels will immerse you in the adventure and its memorable scenes.

Features include:

Compelling Character Driven Story: Shadows of Adam’s story is one with a deep narrative and an interesting plot. The story revolves around 4 main characters: Asrael, Kellan, Curtis and Talon.
A Strategic AP Management Battle System: AP is restored between each round of battle automatically and through defeating enemies. This allows a unique attrition system that encourages skill use and fast combat.
Beautiful Visuals: Shadows of Adam features beautifully modernized visuals inspired by classic JRPGs of the '90s.
Original Soundtrack With Over 44 Tracks: An original soundtrack by Tyler Mire that’s inspired by music from the genre's greatest games. This soundtrack includes unique themes for each area and character and has an emphasis on strong melodies and an emotional connection.

notes.title: Something Classic Games announces TWO new projects!
notes.notes:
Something Classic Games is thrilled to announce the production of two new exciting JRPGs: Quartet and Pillars of Dust. Spearheaded by members from the Shadows of Adam development team, the games will also be developed with new outside collaborators.
 
[u][b]Pillars of Dust:[/b][/u]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/7fc0af19f90c6cef0434f913360c118aa47e36f8.png[/img]

Josh Garlitz (programmer and developer of Shadows of Adam) and Andrew Steadman bring together a JRPG with an arcade feel. Speed through the game as two men on an intersecting quest, or take the time to explore and learn about the storied past of the once prosperous nation of Alluriga. Grinding and repetition take a backseat to exploration, bizarre characters, and jokes about wimpy hands.
 
[b]FEATURES[/b]
   [list]
[*]  Two main quest lines that come together 
[*]     SELECT which order you want to complete the game in: play through one character’s entire arc before starting the other’s. Choose carefully: the order you play in will confer advantages to the other character!
[*]     Unique dialogue and world building: exploration and talking to everyone and everything will be worth your while
[*]     Keep track of your progress as you try to earn the legendary 100% completion
[*]     In game currency is chicken nuggets
[/list]

Pillars of Dust is aiming for a Q1 2020 release on PC. Follow its development on [url=https://twitter.com/retreauxgames?fbclid=IwAR2WbEj7DbOrBL4itGNQ8u-5saTT0vcTe4_IilLAy0cRzusjxzAG46-oNeQ]twitter[/url].

notes.title: Version 1.0.7 patch now out!
notes.notes:
Hi all,

We have a new patch out which includes mostly small QoL and a few fixes.

A big discovery is something that will help all those who have tried streaming with OBS or use a Steam Controller.

If you are using Windows 10, right-click the "Shadows of Adam.exe" executable. Click the 'Compatibility' tab and run the game with Windows 8 compatibility. That should keep the Steam Controller working consistently and allow you to capture SoA with a "Window Capture".

https://www.youtube.com/watch?time_continue=1&v=bjmX7NdJX8w

This might be a potential fix for Steam Link/in-home streaming issues as well. If someone could try this and let us know, we'd appreciate it!

[b]Updates:[/b]
[list]
[*]Support for left analog stick on controllers
[/list]

[b]Fixes:[/b]
[list]
[*]Warfist had wrong accuracy buff assigned. Typo in description fixed.
[*]Sell menu has 10s digit toggling and added SFXs.
[*]Elixir no longer removes positive status such as "Double-Up" or "Blur"
[*]Menu now displays description of currently equipped equipment.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/b423b25235f90acab75a3102ff5e22951bdb024a.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/691b63b9f05d1fc287999cfe49f200b04c4edf1b.png[/img]

notes.title: DLC, Player's Guide and Too Many Games Conference
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

It has been three months since our epic release and we've had an amazing time. To keep the good feelings rollin', we are here to update you all on some new content we will be releasing and announcement of a conference we will be attending!

Our first exciting announcement is that Something Classic will be presenting Shadows of Adam at  [url=http://toomanygames.com/]Too Many Games[/url]  in Philadelphia this month June 23rd-25th at their Indie Show Case!

"TooManyGames is the premier 3 day video game, board game, CCG, music, panel, and tabletop gaming convention event in the Philadelphia area."

If you're in the area, it'd be great to meet you all! We'll be providing demos of the game and perhaps you'll even get to play our new additional content! Speaking of that...

Work has been steady trying to complete our DLC content. Namely the Backer's Guild and the Player's Guide. The Backer's Guild will be bundled with additional content which will be sold as DLC upon completion. The Player's Guide will also be sold via our Steam page for a very low price.

Let's run down what you'll find in the Backer's Guild:

[b]The Black Market:[/b]

Wanna buy rare items and artifacts? The sultry shopkeepers are more than happy to take your coin in exchange for these rare trinkets.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/d72d729b32c21cd0f40f077ede9d1b12f7fe62c6.png[/img]

Introducing 14 new artifacts!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/d6d4b0782164f34eee8363d1145752268f6d5aa2.png[/img]
 

[b]Battle Arena:[/b]

Take on 7 different tiers of monster encounters in a thrilling battle gauntlet with various limitations placed upon the team. The stakes are high, but the rewards are even greater!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/66a803388c347c2be527adae0d2eee1802a817f8.png[/img]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/b81cfdda59141a320a4674c7fe12e73fb41809b2.png[/img]
 
I even wrote some new exciting music for these thrilling battles:
https://soundcloud.com/tm0135/boss-battle?in=tm0135/sets/video-game-music-compositions

[b]Artifact Crafting:[/b]

Combine and craft artifacts to your delight. Want a Fire Badge that increases AP by 50%? This is the place!

In addition we are including even more content in our DLC bundle such as:

[b]New Game Plus/Difficulty Mode:[/b]

Think you got what it takes? Replay SoA with all your end game equipment and artifacts. Your level is reset to 1, but all the monsters get a super buff!

[b]Mystic Caverns:[/b]

Rumor has it there is an ancient cave of the Wraithlings that include some of the world's most powerful relics. Beware though, monsters of unfathomable strength and puzzles of mind busting complexity await!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/88a3027a9ee37d03d45f2c130d7703448e272db4.png[/img]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/d47d80771b7d9bbef51ae2e7aeb88a4a156915e6.png[/img]

 In addition, we have been slowly working our way through the Player's Guide. Here's a few sneak peaks!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/f5803d98d44bd47187a04dc5b2e8ccc9cc8cffec.jpg[/img]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/fce41185d9c357ab481079cdebeede465b392ddf.jpg[/img]

That's it for this update. As always, thank you for your tremendous support!

All the best,
Ty, Tyler, Josh, Tim, and Luke

notes.notes:
SAN FRANCISCO, CA - February 3, 2017 - The team at Something Classic Games are excited to announce that their love letter to the JRPG genre, Shadows of Adam will launch on February 23 for PC/Mac/Linux.

Shadows of Adam tells the story of a legendary hero named Orazio, who abruptly disappears, leaving behind his adopted daughter, son and a dark secret. With darkness looming over the village of Adam and their legendary hero being lost, it’s up to Kellan and Asrael to save their homeland and uncover the truth behind their father’s abrupt disappearance.

“It’s an honor for us to provide Shadows of Adam in its entirety to newcomers, and of course our Kickstarter supporters, followers and fans finally getting their full course meal!” said Something Classic Games Creative Director Tim Wendorf. “This game is our tribute to an industry which has consistently rewarded its followers for decades by offering classic after classic to keep even the strongest and most unique RPG urges satiated.” 

Players will be able to explore diverse handcrafted environments without having to worry about random encounters. Players will also experience a completely unique AP battle system that encourages skill use and fast-paced combat.

For more information on Shadows of Adam visit http://www.shadowsofadam.com and follow @SomethingClassc on Twitter.

notes.title: WEEKLY CONTENT BLOG #55: LEARNING FROM EXPERIENCE
notes.notes:
The other day out of the blue, an old friend sent me a message of Facebook. He was looking for a transcription I did 6 years ago and was wondering if I could sell him the parts so his college band could perform it. Having not looked at the piece in several years, I pulled open the file on my computer to find… awfulness, complete awfulness. The formatting was horrible, the chord voicings were rusty, and the attention to detail I have learned in the past years was not present. I promptly told my friend I would then spend the next few hours polishing up the piece and then I would send it to him. A few hours turned into a day, a day turned into a week, and a week turned into a month. What was acceptable to me 6 years ago, was no longer representative of the quality I try and achieve in 2017. This got me thinking about Shadows of Adam and my role as the composer. Since my first composition in October of 2013 to last week when I updated ZaknNik’s battle theme, I’ve learned a lot.

1.	A little bit of reverb goes a long way
About 2 years in I discovered a small trick to make the pieces sound more coherent. I started running a small amount of reverb through an aux channel. This in turned applied the reverb equally to all instruments giving it a cohesive sound, almost as if all the instruments were being played in the same space. This may seem obvious to most, but my background was always as a composer and not necessarily a sound designer. Once learning this I promptly remixed every tune I had done to that point.

2.	Make the most out of your themes (aka Melody is King)
When writing some of the first pieces for SoA I knew I would want to come up with a handful of themes that could be re-used throughout. I ended up developing two main themes:

–Main Theme
–Curtis’s Theme

From a pragmatic point of view, it made sense to re-use these because it saved me work, however I also felt it helped bring a cohesive story-centric perspective to the game. For instance, the main theme is reworked in a more minor key in a scene to show Asrael’s distress while Curtis’ theme was re-orchestrated to work for Orazio. At times, both themes have been used in counterpoint to help highlight specific story elements.

3.	Panning and Sonic Space 
When mixing your tunes it’s important to give some space in the panning to help instruments come out. If two instruments complement each other or occupy the same register, sometimes panning them straight across from each other can prevent it from sounding muddy. I also learned this trick from listening to old SNES tunes. A lot of times, harmony in the same instrument patch woudl be split into two tracks and panned on opposite sides. This is another way to create a more linear sounds with your instruments as opposed to blocks of sound where each note is hard to distinguish.

4.	Go with your gut 
I am a studied musician. In addition to my 6 years of higher ed (Bachelors and Masters in Music Composition) I have composed over 200 pieces of music for games, jazz ensembles, pop bands, and various other groups. However, I still firmly believe that the best music comes from instinct and imagination. I always try to write things that I can sing because they seem to flow naturally and feel the most musical. The craft I’ve developed is merely a tool I employ to help articulate my musical ideas. That is not to say that I am not challenging myself to learn new harmonies, melodic constructions, or ways to phrase, but that it is ok being comfortable with my instincts. They’ve served me well.

5.	Sleep on it
Sometimes this is the most important thing to do when composing a new piece. Frequently at the start of a new tune I would write as much down as I could come up with. Things would write itself for a bit, then I would inevidently hit a wall. At this point, I would begin to feel that my ideas were becoming forced and that I needed to take a break. I always found a long walk or a day off helped me recharge and come back with more creative juices. Occasionally, on walks with my dog I would replay the song in my head over and over, and imagine all the possibilities for it. This would help me get a good big picture concept and fine tune the ideas I already had. The most extreme example of this was the final boss theme. I started it in Jan of 2014 and finished it in the fall of 2016!

Looking back I am very grateful for the three plus years of writing I’ve done for Shadows of Adam. I’ve grown a lot as a musician and I am very proud of what we all have achieved.

Stay tuned for updates on the official Shadows of Adam release date! If you haven’t done so you can pre-order Shadows of Adam or contact us on our may social media outlets:

www.shadowsofadam.com
www.somethingclassic.net

Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/SomethingClassicGames
Twitter: https://twitter.com/somethingclassc/
Twitch: https://www.twitch.tv/somethingclassic

All the best!
-Tyler

notes.title: Weekly Content Blog #54: Looking Back
notes.notes:
New posts every Wednesday: [url=http://blog.somethingclassic.net/ ] Something Classic Dev Log [/url] 

Some three years since it all began, here I sit, looking back on the journey that has been Shadows of Adam. So it seems appropriate to look back at some of the important lessons I’ve learned along the way.

1. Good dialogue doesn’t just write itself, except when it does.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/2c9a2e77916104f5021116085af6b3311659f996.png[/img]
An example of some particularly stellar writing…

2. You really need a team you can trust. And I do trust in my team. All zero of them I have met in real life.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/5e3af4a91f1cd9e85ac19924d47c567cec9f3171.png[/img]
You know you’re an alcoholic when…

3. You can’t be good at everything, but you can try. And fail. Thank god for the wonders of the division of labor.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/045f16761d54416a723bf47a8c210a84dc7e6aec.png[/img]
Kellan is NOT a good pirate

4. Always be closing. Sure you can make a game, but can you sell it? If you want to quit your day job and make more games, you’ll probably have to. Definitely not the fun part of making a game, but you should have your sales pitch in hand early on.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/2c6942e1c65c43818a4d7ea074e6f24c2b5ed8be.png[/img]
The catchy slogan sell! Always be closing!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/40bdd53d943a400f9724b5f451827b580350c705.png[/img]
The super hard you’ll-die-without-this-product sell. Always be closing!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/cc3f0dbb3f5ace1c53fdceb0ba98f7c39d2ed8fb.png[/img]
The hahaha-there-are-no-slimes-in-the-Misty-Woods-I’m-a-freakin’-liar sell! Always be closing!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26501231/7a85cdd2ee628c59d967a1ada52817b0f06efb4e.png[/img]
The drunk-frat-boy-pickup-line sell? Always be… yeah, not happening.

5. Number three again. You can’t be good at everything, so get help with marketing.

I hope this has been as eye-opening and insightful as my two minutes of deep reflection led me to believe. Until next time.
